units.title: Limits
units.blurb: Understand limits from graphs, compute them with algebra, and define them precisely.

units.title: The Derivative
units.blurb: Go from average to instantaneous rate of change, and define the derivative as a limit.

units.title: Differentiation Rules
units.blurb: Differentiate powers, products, quotients, compositions, and trig, exponential and log functions.

units.title: Applications of Derivatives
units.blurb: Use derivatives for motion, related rates, approximation, graph shape and optimization.

units.title: Integrals
units.blurb: Find antiderivatives, build definite integrals from sums, and use the Fundamental Theorem and substitution.

topics.title: Limits from Both Sides
topics.short: lim f(x) = L when f(x) gets close to L as x gets close to a, from both sides.
topics.trouble: Students think the limit is just f(a), so they say a limit fails to exist wherever f(a) is undefined.

topics.title: One-Sided Limits
topics.short: The two-sided limit exists only when the left and right limits agree.
topics.trouble: Students report a two-sided limit at a jump by using only one side.

topics.title: Infinite Limits and Vertical Asymptotes
topics.short: f(x) can grow without bound near a point.
topics.trouble: Students write lim = ∞ and then treat ∞ as a number in later arithmetic.

topics.title: Limit Laws
topics.short: Limits of sums, products and quotients follow from the limits of the parts.
topics.trouble: Students use the quotient law when the denominator's limit is 0.

topics.title: Limits by Factoring and Canceling
topics.short: Rewrite 0/0 forms to remove the troublesome factor.
topics.trouble: Students conclude that a 0/0 form means the limit is 0 or does not exist.

topics.title: Limits by Rationalizing
topics.short: Multiply by a conjugate to resolve 0/0 forms with roots.

topics.title: The Squeeze Theorem
topics.short: Trap a function between two with the same limit.

topics.title: Special Trigonometric Limits
topics.short: sin(x)/x → 1 and (1 − cos x)/x → 0 as x → 0.
topics.trouble: Students cancel the x in sin(x)/x, or use degrees, where the limit is not 1.

topics.title: Continuity
topics.short: f is continuous at a when the limit equals f(a).
topics.trouble: Students think a function is continuous wherever it is defined, missing jumps in piecewise functions.

topics.title: The Intermediate Value Theorem
topics.short: A continuous function that changes sign must hit 0 in between.
topics.trouble: Students apply the theorem to a function that is not continuous on the interval.

topics.title: Limits at Infinity and Horizontal Asymptotes
topics.short: Compare the growth of the highest powers.
topics.trouble: Students treat ∞/∞ as 1 or ∞ − ∞ as 0.

topics.title: The Precise Definition of a Limit
topics.short: For every ε > 0 there is a δ > 0 that keeps f(x) within ε of L.
topics.trouble: Students choose ε after δ, reversing the order of the quantifiers.

topics.title: From Average to Instantaneous Rate
topics.short: Shrink the interval of an average rate to get a rate at an instant.

topics.title: The Derivative at a Point
topics.short: f′(a) is the limit of the difference quotient: the slope of the tangent line.
topics.trouble: Students expand f(a + h) as f(a) + h, or plug in h = 0 before simplifying.

topics.title: Tangent Lines
topics.short: Use f′(a) as the slope of the line y = f(a) + f′(a)(x − a).
topics.trouble: Students use f′(x) instead of the number f′(a) as the slope.

topics.title: The Derivative as a Function
topics.short: f′ gives the slope of f at every x.
topics.trouble: Students sketch f′ to look like f, instead of tracking where f rises, falls and levels off.

topics.title: Where Derivatives Fail to Exist
topics.short: Corners, cusps, vertical tangents and breaks.
topics.trouble: Students think every continuous function is differentiable.

topics.title: Leibniz Notation and Units
topics.short: dy/dx is a rate with units of y per unit of x.
topics.trouble: Students give the units of the derivative as the units of y.

topics.title: Constant, Power and Sum Rules
topics.short: d/dx xⁿ = nxⁿ⁻¹, and derivatives split over sums.
topics.trouble: Students apply the power rule to 2ˣ, writing x·2ˣ⁻¹.

topics.title: The Product Rule
topics.short: (fg)′ = f′g + fg′.
topics.trouble: Students write (fg)′ = f′g′.

topics.title: The Quotient Rule
topics.short: (f/g)′ = (f′g − fg′)/g².
topics.trouble: Students reverse the order of the numerator, which flips the sign.

topics.title: Derivatives of Trig Functions
topics.short: d/dx sin x = cos x and d/dx cos x = −sin x.
topics.trouble: Students drop the minus sign on the derivative of cos x.

topics.title: Higher Derivatives
topics.short: Differentiate again to get f″, f‴ and beyond.

topics.title: The Chain Rule
topics.trouble: Students forget to multiply by the derivative of the inside function.

topics.title: Chain Rule with Several Layers
topics.short: Peel a composition from the outside in.
topics.trouble: Students stop after two layers, or differentiate an inner layer twice.

topics.title: Derivatives of Exponential and Log Functions
topics.short: d/dx eˣ = eˣ and d/dx ln x = 1/x.
topics.trouble: Students write d/dx e^(3x) = e^(3x), forgetting the chain rule factor 3.

topics.title: Implicit Differentiation
topics.short: Differentiate both sides, treating y as a function of x.
topics.trouble: Students differentiate y² as 2y instead of 2y · dy/dx.

topics.title: Derivatives of Inverse Functions and Inverse Trig
topics.short: d/dx sin⁻¹ x = 1/√(1 − x²).
topics.trouble: Students use 1/f′(x) instead of 1/f′(f⁻¹(x)).

topics.title: Logarithmic Differentiation
topics.short: Take ln of both sides to handle powers like xˣ.
topics.trouble: Students differentiate xˣ with the power rule or the exponential rule alone.

topics.title: Position, Velocity and Acceleration
topics.short: Velocity is the derivative of position; acceleration is the derivative of velocity.
topics.trouble: Students think negative acceleration always means slowing down.

topics.title: Related Rates
topics.short: Differentiate an equation linking quantities to connect their rates.
topics.trouble: Students substitute the given values before differentiating, turning changing quantities into constants.

topics.title: Linear Approximation and Differentials
topics.short: Near a, f(x) ≈ f(a) + f′(a)(x − a).

topics.title: Critical Points and Absolute Extrema
topics.short: Check critical points and endpoints on a closed interval.
topics.trouble: Students assume every critical point is a maximum or minimum, or forget the endpoints.

topics.title: The Mean Value Theorem
topics.short: Somewhere the instantaneous rate equals the average rate.
topics.trouble: Students apply the theorem to a function that is not differentiable on the open interval.

topics.title: Increasing, Decreasing and the First Derivative Test
topics.short: The sign of f′ tells where f rises or falls.
topics.trouble: Students find where f′ = 0 but never test the sign on each side.

topics.title: Concavity and the Second Derivative Test
topics.short: The sign of f″ tells which way the graph bends.
topics.trouble: Students call every point where f″ = 0 an inflection point, without checking a sign change.

topics.title: Curve Sketching
topics.short: Combine limits, f′ and f″ to sketch a graph.

topics.title: Optimization
topics.short: Model a quantity, then find its largest or smallest value.
topics.trouble: Students optimize the wrong function or ignore the realistic domain.

topics.title: L'Hôpital's Rule
topics.short: For 0/0 or ∞/∞, compare the derivatives of the numerator and denominator.
topics.trouble: Students apply the quotient rule to the fraction, or use the rule on limits that are not indeterminate.

topics.title: Newton's Method
topics.short: Use tangent lines to approach a root.

topics.title: Antiderivatives
topics.short: Run differentiation backward, and add the constant C.
topics.trouble: Students forget + C, or integrate xⁿ as xⁿ⁺¹ without dividing.

topics.title: Antiderivatives with Initial Conditions
topics.short: Use a known value to find C.

topics.title: Approximating Area with Rectangles
topics.short: Add up rectangle areas to estimate the area under a curve.
topics.trouble: Students use the wrong endpoints for left and right sums.

topics.title: Riemann Sums
topics.short: A sum of f(xᵢ)Δx approximates the area; more rectangles do better.

topics.title: The Definite Integral
topics.short: The limit of Riemann sums gives net signed area.
topics.trouble: Students treat every definite integral as total area and ignore parts below the axis.

topics.title: Properties of Definite Integrals
topics.short: Split intervals, reverse limits and compare integrals.

topics.title: Accumulation Functions and FTC Part 1
topics.short: d/dx ∫ₐˣ f(t) dt = f(x).
topics.trouble: Students forget the chain rule factor when the upper limit is a function of x.

topics.title: Evaluating Integrals with FTC Part 2
topics.short: ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a).
topics.trouble: Students compute F(a) − F(b), or drop a minus sign when F(a) is negative.

topics.title: Net Change and Total Distance
topics.short: The integral of a rate gives net change; total distance needs |v|.
topics.trouble: Students report displacement when total distance is asked.

topics.title: Average Value of a Function
topics.short: f_avg = (1/(b − a)) ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx.

topics.title: Integration by Substitution
topics.short: Reverse the chain rule by choosing u = inside function.
topics.trouble: Students leave a mix of x and u in the integral, or forget to account for du.

topics.title: Substitution in Definite Integrals
topics.short: Change the limits to match u.
topics.trouble: Students change the variable but keep the old limits of integration.

topics.title: Integrals Giving Exponentials and Logarithms
topics.short: ∫ 1/x dx = ln|x| + C and ∫ eˣ dx = eˣ + C.
topics.trouble: Students drop the absolute value in ln|x|, or apply ∫ 1/x dx to 1/x².

topics.title: Integrals Giving Inverse Trig Functions
topics.short: ∫ 1/(1 + x²) dx = tan⁻¹ x + C.
topics.trouble: Students write ln(1 + x²) for ∫ 1/(1 + x²) dx.
